summary: Discovery focused on cost/unit economics. Customer currently uses hosted endpoints from other providers; main concerns are per-token cost at scale, ability to use batching and KV/prefix caching to meet budget, and whether Dedicated or Private gives better unit economics given their throughput and latency SLOs. Agreed next steps: share pricing + security docs, run benchmark on sample workload, and set up a 1-week pilot.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 38 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Carlos Nguyen (Redwood SE), Lena Morris (Pegasus Head of ML), Tom Becker (Pegasus SRE), Ravi Shah (Pegasus VP Eng)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I think we have about 40 minutes, want to focus on cost economics and what a pilot might look like, so quick intros?
[00:15] Lena: Hey, Lena here, head of ML at Pegasus. We run a mix of LLM workloads for research ops and production trading signals, mostly open models on other vendors.
[00:25] Ravi: Ravi, VP Eng. We're looking at budget impact, monthly run-rate, and compliance constraints.
[00:35] Tom: Tom, SRE. Interested in throughput, latency SLOs, and how batching will affect tail latency.
[00:45] Maya: Great. Carlos from our infra team will cover batching and caching details.
[00:50] Carlos: Hi all, quick high-level — Redwood offers hosted, dedicated, and private. For cost math we care about per-token pricing, batching, prefix/KV caching, and autoscaling granularity.

[01:20] Maya: Can you give us a sense of current volume and patterns? tokens per request, percent of long-context, pct of realtime vs batch?
[01:35] Lena: Sure. Roughly 8M tokens/day across prod and staging. 70% are short prompts (<256 tokens) but we have a heavy tail — maybe 8% are >2k tokens for multi-doc summarization. Peak qps ~220 requests/sec during market hours. Budget target $35k/month for hosted inference.
[02:05] Maya: Nice, that helps. So naive per-token math matters. For our hosted endpoint our list price is X per 1k tokens, but effective unit cost depends on batching and cache hit rates.

[02:40] Tom: Quick question — when you say batching, does that increase latency? Our SLO for trading is <200ms P95.
[02:50] Carlos: Good callout. Continuous batching trades a bit of latency for throughput; we can configure max latency windows and per-route low-latency paths. For strict <200ms we often recommend pinning to smaller batch sizes or using Dedicated capacity sized for concurrency.

[03:30] Lena: So dedicated sounds like predictable cost, but how does that compare to hosted per-token? If we reserve GPUs, what are the amortized costs?
[03:45] Carlos: With Dedicated you pay for reserved capacity (monthly commit) but you get much better unit economics at high sustained throughput because you avoid multi-tenant markup and can tune quantization/sequence length to squeeze cost. We typically model two scenarios: hosted pay-as-you-go vs dedicated reserved. For your 8M tokens/day, at our hosted list price the monthly runs about ~X (we'll send exact numbers), dedicated could lower per-token by 20-40% depending on utilization and batching.

[04:30] Ravi: Is that 20-40% after including operational overheads and support?
[04:40] Maya: Yes includes standard support and observability. Private (VPC) adds platform fees but is comparable to Dedicated once you factor in infra costs.

[05:05] Tom: On caching — what types do you offer? Prefix and KV? How would that impact our multi-doc summarization flows?
[05:15] Carlos: We have prefix caching for repeated prefixes and KV cache for incremental decoding reuse. For workflows where the beginning of the prompt repeats (system prompts, templates) you can get very high hit rates; for multi-doc summarization we recommend chunk-level KV caching plus response-level reuse — depends on your prompt design. Typical hit rates vary; we've seen 10-60% effective token savings depending on workload.

[06:00] Lena: Hmm 10-60% is a big range. How do you recommend estimating for us?
[06:10] Carlos: Send us 7-day token histograms and a few example prompts; we run a quick sim to estimate cache hit and batching gains. That gives concrete percent savings to plug into cost model.

[06:35] Maya: Also important: quantization and model selection. Smaller quantized variants can cut cost but risk quality regressions — we can help run A/B quality checks.

[07:05] Ravi: For budgeting, we need deterministic worst-case. How do fallbacks work if Dedicated capacity is saturated?
[07:15] Carlos: We offer smart routing and automatic fallback to hosted pool or other model variants — you can set policy priorities. Fallback can increase latency or cost depending on route.

[07:45] Tom: On the SRE side, how does autoscaling work? We can't have a thaw of GPUs spinning up mid-market hours.
[07:55] Carlos: Dedicated supports aggressive pre-warm and predictable autoscale policies; you configure headroom thresholds, and we can coordinate with your ops to avoid cold starts.

[08:20] Lena: Can you walk through a sample cost calc live? Even ballpark is useful.
[08:28] Maya: Sure — say 8M tokens/day * 30 = 240M tokens/month. At hosted list price of $0.0012 per 1k tokens (example) naive is ~288 USD? wait, math oops — let me restate: 240M tokens is 240k 1k-token units; at $0.12 per 1k tokens that'd be $28.8k. Sorry we use different granularities, we'll send a spreadsheet. The key is effective cost = list * (1 - cache_hit) * (1 - batching_efficiency).
[09:15] Lena: Ok that aligns with our $35k target if we can hit caching and batching.

[09:30] Ravi: How do you measure batching efficiency? It's not linear.
[09:38] Carlos: Right — batching efficiency is measured as saved compute per token vs single inference. Continuous batching with similar sequence lengths gives better GPU utilization; we model utilization curves per model. We'll include curves in the deck.

[10:05] Tom: Another ops question — encryption and KMS support? We need customer-managed keys for Private.
[10:14] Maya: Yes, Private and Dedicated integrate with KMS/HSM, full audit logs and SOC2 controls. We can provide the security package.

[10:40] Lena: If we do a 1-week pilot, what telemetry do you need?
[10:47] Carlos: Ideally: 7-day token hist, median/95/99 latencies, typical prompt samples, and a small eval set for quality checks. We'll run perf benchmarks and produce tokens/cost per-run numbers.

[11:10] Ravi: On contract terms — what's minimum committed for Dedicated?
[11:18] Maya: Typical is monthly or annual reserved. We can start with a small monthly commit for pilot. Terms flexible based on usage and forecast.

[11:40] Lena: Is there a way to cap spend if experiments blow up?
[11:45] Maya: Yes, we have per-route quotas and global hard caps you can set. We also emit token-level billing so you can detect anomalies quickly.

[12:05] Tom: Flex on dry-run benchmarks — can Carlos show example results you've done for similar quant finance customers?
[12:12] Carlos: I can share anonymized benchmark spreadsheets — throughput, p95 latency, and cost per 1k tokens across modes. I have one from a hedge fund customer that had similar QPS — showed 30% cost savings moving to Dedicated with caching.

[12:40] Lena: One more thing — for our multi-doc summarization we need context windows >4k often. How does longer context affect pricing?
[12:50] Carlos: Longer context increases token compute linearly; cost is per input+output token. But caching KV for repeated history and chunking strategies help. Also model kernel selection matters for long seq performance; Dedicated lets us pick optimized kernels/quantization.

[13:30] Ravi: Can you do a product demo? Maybe next call.
[13:35] Maya: Absolutely — we'll schedule a 45-min demo + SE deep dive.

[13:45] Tom: For the pilot, can we try dedicated reservation for a week? Even a small pool?
[13:52] Maya: Yes, we can provision a small dedicated pool for a week for benchmarking. We'll need an internal purchase order or approval to spin up for private infra — if Hosted Dedicated it's simpler.

[14:20] Lena: Any potential gotchas? E.g., tokenization differences across models or small hidden costs?
[14:30] Carlos: Tokenization differences can change effective token counts by ~5-15% across models. We'll token-compare your prompts across model variants. Also network egress and long-term storage can add costs in Private. We'll surface all of that.

[15:00] Maya: OK I'll summarize next steps. We'll send a pricing spreadsheet with hosted vs dedicated vs private comparisons, include modeled caching/batching scenarios, and security docs. Carlos will run a perf benchmark on your sample prompts once Lena shares histograms.
[15:20] Lena: Sounds good. Can you also include an example math table showing worst-case and expected-case monthly spend?
[15:30] Maya: Yes.

[15:40] Ravi: Timeline-wise we want to decide in 2 weeks, any blockers?
[15:45] Maya: No blockers, just need your sample data and a quick PO for pilot if you want dedicated reserved.

[16:05] Tom: Ok thanks everyone.
[16:10] Maya: Thanks, we'll follow up by Friday with docs and proposed pilot dates.
[16:18] Carlos: Bye all.

[38:00] End of recording.
